title: Sonny Gray reportedly interested in signing extension with Red Sox
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Sonny Gray, 36, has expressed interest in a contract extension with the Boston Red Sox after a strong 2026 season.
Gray boasts a 12-2 record with a 2.78 ERA, contributing to Boston's 18-4 record in July, now playoff contenders.
Boston considers re-signing Gray, who may attract lucrative offers, for stability as younger pitchers emerge in rotation.

title: Teen driver killed, 4 others hospitalized in stolen SUV crash in Abington
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: A 17-year-old driver died in a stolen SUV crash in Abington, Massachusetts on Wednesday morning.
Four passengers, aged 14 to 17, were hospitalized with serious injuries after the vehicle hit a tree.
The crash occurred during a police attempt to stop the stolen Hyundai Santa Fe at 877 Washington St.

title: Celtics ‘expressed interest’ in LeBron James in free agency before he joined 76ers
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: The Boston Celtics were interested in LeBron James during free agency, though he ultimately chose the Philadelphia 76ers.
LeBron James signed a two-year deal with the Philadelphia 76ers, joining with Jaylen Brown and Joel Embiid.
At 41, LeBron James averaged 20.9 points, 6.1 rebounds, and 7.2 assists with the Lakers before exiting.

title: Parts of Mass. under flash flood warning as state sees heavy rain
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: Flash flood warning issued until 6 p.m. for Springfield, Chicopee, and Westfield in Western Massachusetts.
Berkshire County under a flood warning until 5:45 p.m., with possible rainfall totals up to 7 inches.
Central, Western Massachusetts, Eastern Rhode Island, and Connecticut under flood watch until 8 p.m. due to continuous rainfall.

title: Cyclist, 39, killed in Stoughton crash
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: Mark Salvador, 39, was killed in a crash while cycling on Washington St. in Stoughton early Wednesday morning.
Stoughton police found Salvador after he was struck by a vehicle; he was pronounced dead an hour later at a Boston hospital.
The Norfolk County DA is investigating the crash; no driver details or potential charges have been disclosed.

title: Wu unveiled a street safety plan after a cyclist was killed. Transit advocates say it doesn’t go far enough.
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Mayor Michelle Wu announced street safety plans after cyclist Louisa Gag was killed on Tremont Street.
Wu's plan includes quick-build barriers and urban design evaluations but lacks specific timelines and accountability.
Transit advocates criticize Wu's proposals as insufficient, urging for detailed actions and accountability on paused projects.

title: What to know about the Green Line shutdowns planned for August
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: MBTA will suspend Green Line service from Aug. 8 to 16 between key points for tunnel upgrades.
Free shuttles and bus services will replace suspended Green Line B, C, D, and E branches.
Symphony Station remains closed for upgrades until 2029; additional temporary station closures are planned.

title: Suffolk corrections officer killed after stopping to help stranded motorist in Boxford
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Brett Martin, a 51-year-old Suffolk corrections officer, was killed while helping a stranded motorist on I-95 in Boxford.
Massachusetts State Police reported that Martin was struck by a vehicle at 8:30 p.m. and later died at a hospital.
The Essex County District Attorney’s Office is investigating the incident, and Martin's department praised his dedication and bravery.

title: Review & setlist: Tame Impala reimagines the bounds of arena rock at TD Garden
author: Perry Eaton
bullets: Tame Impala performed at TD Garden, drawing capacity crowds for two nights with a 360-degree stage setup.
Opener Djo, featuring Newburyport native Joe Keery, impressed with tracks from his latest album, The Crux.
Tame Impala's show combined psychedelic and house influences, incorporating elaborate visuals and a diverse setlist.

title: Electric utility rates are going up Aug. 1. Will your bill actually increase?
author: Annie Jonas
bullets: Massachusetts electric utility rates will increase on August 1, impacting National Grid, Eversource, and Unitil customers on basic service.
Eversource's basic service rate rises from 15.6 to 17.3 cents per kWh, National Grid from 15.546 to 16.074 cents per kWh.
Only 26.6% of Massachusetts electric customers on basic service will directly experience the rate hike, others use alternate suppliers.
